Description: Seattle businesses open to the public that started 50+ years ago (before about November 1976). Every one appears on the City of Seattle’s active business license list.

Places in Seattle on the National Register of Historic Places that still exist: buildings, historic districts, bridges, parks, ships and sites. Demolished or destroyed listings are left out. The year shown is when a place was added to the Register, not when it was built.

Public stairways in Seattle's streets and rights-of-way, from the Seattle Department of Transportation's stairway inventory. Step counts and condition come from SDOT's inspections; closed stairways are included and marked. The year, where known, is when the stairway was built.

Seattle Municipal Street Railway streetcar and cable car routes from the railway's own list, “Streetcar routes – April 1st, 1931,” close to the network's greatest extent. Each route is drawn outbound along today's streets, so stretches where streets have since changed are approximate. Click a line or pick a route to see its 1931 streets. Not drawn: the Seahurst shuttle (4s) from White Center to Lake Burien, whose streets the list doesn't give.
